taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.culm_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 332, Carex mertensii: "Cespitose and short stoloniferous, the culms 3-10 dm. high, sharply triangular, rough".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 332, Carex mertensii: "Leaf-blades flat, 4-7 mm. wide, the lower sheaths brownish purple tinged".

appearance.organs.panicle.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 332, Carex mertensii: "spikes 6-10, gynaecandrous" ... "1-4 cm. long, 7-10 mm. wide, the upper approximate, the lower more remote on capillary peduncles, the perigynia numerous, appressed-ascending"; perigynia "light green, purple spotted"; scales "brown with light midvein and margins". Drawn as a raceme of 8 spikes, each about 3 cm by 9 mm on a thread-like stalk that droops, the light green perigynia over brown scales.

generator.params.note: Dewey's and slough sedges' values, changed by hand for Mertens's sedge: a loose tuft of flat leaves shorter than the culms, the culms rising above them and nodding under their drooping spikes (Abrams 1923 p. 332). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.7 m tall at 4 years in the open, inside Abrams's 3-10 dm culms. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1923 p. 332): green leaves over "brownish purple tinged" lower sheaths; light green spikes flecked brown by their scales.
